newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope enters hospital for appendix operation.
newsitem.headline: Pope enters hospital for appendix operation.

text.p: Pope John Paul arrived on Sunday at the Gemelli hospital in Rome where he will have an operation to remove his appendix, reporters at the scene said.

The Pope, 76, was to be met by Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and senior Gemelli staff before being accompanied to a special 10th floor suite with its own chapel. Hospital officials said the operation was expected to be carried out on Tuesday.

It will be the Polish-born Pontiff's sixth stay at the Gemelli, where he had major abdominal surgery twice after being shot in an assassination attempt in 1981 and again in 1992 to remove a colon tumour which was starting to turn malignant.
The Vatican announced the latest operation last month when it said recurrent inflammation of the appendix was the cause of three bouts of "intestinal fever" the Pope has suffered since Christmas.
Its statement has been met with scepticism by many doctors, some of whom have speculated that the Pope may have another tumour. The Vatican has denied such reports.
